## Per-gate requirement specs

Every structural sub-gate publishes a **proactive requirement contract**
so you can author-to-contract *before* pushing rather than learning the
requirement from red CI. Read one gate's contract with
`gyrum-gate-spec <gate>` (`--all` for the set, `--json` for machine use).
This table is generated from `lib/gates-catalogue.json`; the meta-gate
refuses any gate that ships without a complete spec.

| Gate | Requires | Satisfy (proactively) | Spec |
|------|----------|-----------------------|------|
| `claude-stub-integrity` | every CLAUDE.md gyrum-*-vN:START marker that declares detail=<path>@vN has that <path> present and carrying a matching gyrum-*-detail-vN stamp | run gyrum-setup --sync-claudemd to (re)write the docs/gyrum/*.md companions, or fix the detail= path/version in the stub marker | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `conformance` | for every migrated area (a directory carrying a committed OpenAPI spec) that the diff TOUCHES, the area's Go conformance test (cmd/server/<area>/conformance_test.go — the warp#8540 four-check harness driven off the area's CoveredRoutes() registry) passes. DIFF-SCOPED: an area whose spec the diff does not touch — and any un-migrated area carrying no spec — is NOT checked. ADVISORY (rc 0) by default; BLOCKING (rc 1, record_fail) under the gyrum-service profile (GYRUM_CONFORMANCE_GATE_HARD=1, warp#8554) when a touched area's conformance test fails. | run `go test ./cmd/server/<area>/ -run Conformance` locally and align the area's openapi.yaml and handlers so every spec op has a handler, every handler maps to a spec op, and request/response shapes validate against the spec; the spec is the contract clients build against. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |

Activation keys on DEPLOYMENT, not repo class (warp#10498): a repo served behind the shared Caddy edge is gated even when tier:personal and even when it carries its own playwright smoke spec — the static scan additionally sweeps the full built output (app.html-derived template(s) + built HTML on disk), not just diff-changed files, because warp#974 smoke drives a CSP-free dev server and cannot catch a CSP-blocked asset baked into app.html. Repos NOT behind the fleet CSP that carry their own playwright smoke spec are SKIPped (warp#974 owns console-clean). | `structural-lockfile` | if a changed package.json alters dependency fields (dependencies / devDependencies / peerDependencies / optionalDependencies / workspaces) the same diff must update a lockfile (package-lock.json / pnpm-lock.yaml / yarn.lock); and any lockfile change must be accompanied by a package.json change. Scripts/metadata-only package.json edits are exempt. | after editing package.json dependency fields run `pnpm install` (or `npm install` / `yarn install`) and commit the regenerated lockfile in the same PR; never hand-edit a lockfile. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-no-conflicts` | `git diff --check BASE...HEAD` exits 0 — no unresolved conflict markers or whitespace errors in the diff. | resolve the merge conflict (remove the <<<<<<< / ======= / >>>>>>> markers) and fix the flagged whitespace before pushing. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-shell-size` | no non-test shell file over 1200 lines grows or newly crosses 1200 lines; shell files over 800 lines warn. | keep a shell file over 1200 lines the same size or smaller and put the new logic in a Go command or package (docs/HOWTO/shell-size-gate.md). | `docs/HOWTO/shell-size-gate.md` |
| `structural-size` | the PR diff stays under the size cap: SIGNAL at 800 changed lines (warning + a splitting-justification phrase), hard BLOCK at 3000. | split the change into a stack of smaller PRs (one concern each); if genuinely indivisible, state why in the PR body using one of the justification phrases (atomic, indivisible, cohesive unit, single concern, splitting would). On the FIRST review pass (before the PR exists) put the justification in the prepared body file .gyrum/pr-body.md (or .gyrum/pr-body-<ticket>.md) — the tooling publishes it with the PR and the gate reads it from there (warp#13254). | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `adapter-source-link` | every devtools lib/*.sh that defines an adapter-forwarder default `: "${<NAME>_CMD:=<adapter>}"` carries an `# adapter-source: <repo> <path> ... build: <cmd>` comment within ~6 lines above the default, naming the repo the adapter is built from and how to build it. | add a comment like `# adapter-source: gyrum-go cmd/<name> (warp#NNNN) — build: (cd ~/work/gyrum-labs/gyrum-go && go build -o ~/.local/bin/<name> ./cmd/<name>)` above the `: "${<NAME>_CMD:=...}"` default, and make the adapter's not-found error path reference it. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `go-apidiff` | for every Go package declared in the repo's ROOT repo-type.yaml `go_api_packages:` list that the PR diff touches (a `*.go` under that package's dir), `apidiff -incompatible <api-at-merge-base> <package-on-branch>` reports no INCOMPATIBLE change — i.e. no removed/retyped exported symbol. Additive changes (a new exported symbol) are compatible and pass. Phase A is warn-only: an incompatible change is a ⚠ advisory row and the gate returns 0 (it hardens to a ✗ block under GO_APIDIFF_ENFORCE=1, Phase B). A repo with NO go_api_packages, no go.mod, or a diff touching no declared package, is a single advisory row that never blocks; apidiff is the pinned single Go binary (no network). | follow expand-contract: add the new exported symbol, migrate every cross-importing trunk, THEN remove/retype the old symbol in a later PR — never a big-bang removal. To verify locally before pushing, run `gyrum-review-pr` (runs this gate) or `go install golang.org/x/exp/cmd/apidiff@v0.0.0-20260611194520-c48552f49976` then `apidiff -w /tmp/base.api <import-path>` at the merge-base checkout and `apidiff -incompatible /tmp/base.api <import-path>` on the branch; fix each finding by restoring the removed/retyped symbol or splitting the change behind the consumer migration. The audited --skip-go-apidiff exists only for a deliberate, consumer-migrated removal the static diff cannot see. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `no-direct-github` | no changed (non-allowlisted) source file (.sh/.go/.ts/.js/.py/.rb/.ya?ml) adds a line performing DIRECT GitHub API egress — `gh api`/`gh graphql`, raw HTTP to api.github.com or uploads.github.com, a github.com/google/go-github import, or an @octokit/ client. Comment-only mentions and docs/markdown are not scanned. Phase A is warn-only: a direct call is a ⚠ advisory row and the gate returns 0 (it hardens to a ✗ block under NO_DIRECT_GITHUB_ENFORCE=1, Phase B, after the warp#9426 broker cutover). Sanctioned direct egress (the github-broker client; CI's installation-token mint) is path-allowlisted in lib/no-direct-github-gate.sh. | route the call through the github-broker (warp#9346) — $GITHUB_BROKER_URL/v1/github/<path> via the broker client — which holds the token pool, enforces the global token-bucket budget, circuit-breaks on secondary-limit 403s, and caches GETs; a broker-routed call contains none of the direct-egress markers so it passes. For a genuinely-sanctioned direct call (the broker client itself, or CI's installation-token mint that must authenticate TO the broker) add its path to _NO_DIRECT_GITHUB_ALLOWLIST, or take the audited override --skip-no-direct-github '<reason >= 20 chars>'. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `a11y-check` | in a repo whose repo-type.yaml declares a design_system block, the Storybook build completes and every story passes the axe-core WCAG 2.1 A/AA audit with no unscoped violations — a violation scoped by the documented warp#10580-precedent header (canon token debt tracked in its own ticket) is not a failure. A repo with no design_system block is a clean no-op. | repair the violation (markup/ARIA/contrast fix in the component), or scope it with the warp#10580-precedent header naming the tracking ticket when it is canon token debt. Re-run the review to confirm the story passes. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `buildinfo` | in a repo with a repo-root VERSION anchor, every build stamp (web-app footer, portal, binary --version, image label) derives its version from that anchor + git HEAD via lib/buildinfo.sh — not from a hand-kept package.json version or hardcoded string whose major.minor differs from the anchor. buildinfo_gate exits 1 and prints → reference/build-identity.md when a package.json version (root or docs-portal/frontend/web/ui/app) normalises to a different major.minor than the anchor, or a hardcoded vX.Y.Z in a build/footer file does not match. | derive the version from the repo VERSION anchor and the commit from git HEAD (pass them into the build as MERIDIAN_VERSION / BUILD_COMMIT build args), keeping package.json only as a last-resort fallback — see reference/build-identity.md (the PoC). Check locally: `lib/buildinfo-gate.sh <repo-root>`. | `reference/build-identity.md` |
| `ci-diff-scope` | a PR that adds/modifies a .github/workflows/*.yml\|yaml must NOT leave an expensive job unscoped in a push- or pull_request-triggered workflow. A job is EXPENSIVE (objective-first) when it declares a services: block, its steps launch browsers/e2e tooling (playwright/cypress/puppeteer/selenium/webkit/chromium/--with-deps/e2e), it declares a strategy: matrix: fan-out, OR (name-heuristic fallback) its id/name matches a heavy class (test/e2e/smoke/contract/integration/api-db/web-e2e/matrix/objective-p50/classifier/browser/playwright/nightly/load-test/benchmark). Each such job must carry a diff-scope guard: EITHER the trigger declares a paths:/paths-ignore: filter, OR the job carries a job-level if: that consults a changed-paths classifier (a needs.<triage>.outputs.<x> reference or a changed-files token). A workflow triggered only by schedule/workflow_dispatch/release etc. is exempt (it cannot fan out per branch). A PR touching no workflow file is a clean ✓ skip and is never inspected. | scope every heavy job to the change it depends on. Preferred (job-level, trigger-agnostic): add a fast changed-scope triage job that emits code_changed/docs_only/changelog_only outputs, then gate each heavy job with `needs: [changed-scope]` + `if: needs.changed-scope.outputs.code_changed == 'true'`, plus an always-run status aggregator so the required check still resolves green when the heavy job is if-skipped (the branch-protection trap). Coarser alternative: add `on.pull_request.paths` / `on.push.paths` (or paths-ignore) to the trigger so the whole workflow only runs for a relevant changed-path set. Verify locally before pushing: source lib/ci-diff-scope-gate.sh and run `check_ci_diff_scope_gate <base> HEAD` — it exits 0 and prints the heavy-jobs-all-scoped row when satisfied. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `ci-workflow-cli-dependency` | a PR that adds/modifies a .github/workflows/*.yml\|yaml whose `run:` shell steps invoke a fleet CLI (any command whose first token matches `^(gyrum-\|warp-)[a-z0-9][-a-z0-9]*`) is flagged when the runner image is not known to provision that CLI. The runner provision source of truth is `.gyrum/runner-provision.yaml` (a `fleet_cli_bins:` list); when present, the gate cross-checks each fleet-CLI reference against it. When absent, the gate emits an advisory per reference (the author must verify the CLI is provisioned). Phase A (default) is advisory-only and never blocks; Phase B (CI_WORKFLOW_CLI_DEPENDENCY_ENFORCE=1) refuses. A PR touching no workflow file is a clean skip. | either provision the fleet CLI on the runner golden image AND list it in .gyrum/runner-provision.yaml's fleet_cli_bins (so every workflow can rely on it); OR use raw API (curl) in the step instead of the CLI — the documented CI-glue exception to the use-the-CLI rule (verb-anti-patterns.yaml targets AGENTS bypassing the CLI for general work, not CI workflows doing deterministic single-shape operations). Verify locally: source lib/ci-workflow-cli-dependency-gate.sh and run `check_ci_workflow_cli_dependency_gate <base> HEAD`. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `cli-doc-pair` | a repo whose declared type OWES cli-doc-pair (the `cli` row of lib/type-gates-map.yaml — declared via repo-type.yaml `type: cli`) must ship a documented command surface: (1) a README.md at the repo root, (2) a docs/userguide.md, and (3) --help coverage — every CLI command under bin/ carries a cli@v3 `# @usage:` tag (so gyrum-help / the generated command-reference covers the VERB), and every long-flag a command HANDLES in its arg parser (a `--name)` case branch) is declared by a matching `# @flag` tag (so --help covers the FLAG, never omitting one the command silently accepts; the universal --help/--version need no tag). A repo of any other / unknown / undeclared type is a clean ✓ n/a row and is never inspected (fail-closed on membership — never enforces on everything). | add a README.md + docs/userguide.md to the cli repo, and document every bin/ command with cli@v3 doc tags — a `# @desc:` + `# @usage:` per command and a `# @flag <token>: <desc>` for each handled long-flag (the same tags gyrum-gen-cli-docs renders into docs/command-reference.md + the gyrum-help table). Verify locally: `bash $DEVTOOLS/lib/cli-doc-pair-gate.sh --self-test <repo-root>` — it prints the gate row and exits 0 when README + userguide + --help coverage all hold. Backfilling an existing undocumented CLI is the documented follow-up; declaring `type: cli` opts the repo into the gate. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `design-doc-completeness` | a repo whose repo-type.yaml declares a design_system block carries all four fleet standard §1 files: src/lib/styles/tokens.css, docs/design/brand-colours.md, docs/design-system.md, and canon-manifest.yaml. A repo with no design_system block is a clean no-op. | restore the missing file (or move the declaration with the rename in the same PR) — the other design gates read these files. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `design-system` | in a repo whose repo-type.yaml declares design_system.source=local, every file matching design_system.scopes keeps its <style>/CSS body free of raw colour literals (#rrggbb, rgb/rgba/hsl/hsla), font-size literals (Npx/Nrem not var()), and dangling var(--<token_prefix>-X) references not defined in design_system.tokens — i.e. `check-design-system.sh --root . --check` reports 0 findings. With enforcement: warn the gate is advisory (exits 0); with enforcement: block a non-zero finding count exits 1. A repo with no design_system block, or source != local, is a clean no-op. | replace the raw value with a token: define the colour/size in design_system.tokens as a `--<token_prefix>-…` custom property and reference it via `var(--<token_prefix>-…)` in the component/route CSS; fix any dangling token by adding its definition to the tokens file or correcting the reference. Check locally: `bash scripts/check-design-system.sh --root . --check`. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `doc-pair` | a PR that adds scripts/<name>.sh, an ansible/roles/<name>/ directory, or a ticket-filing workflow also lands its matching docs: README-<name>.md + HOWTO or runbook for scripts; a role README for ansible roles; a runbook for ticket-filing workflows. | add the companion doc the gate names (README + HOWTO for the script, role README, or workflow runbook), or move the helper into lib/ if it is genuinely internal. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `multi-tenant-boundary` | a PR that touches backend handler/route Go code in a repo that enforces owner-isolation (contains an Owns<Entity>( ownership-check idiom) must carry a tenant-boundary test (a file named *tenant*boundary* or under a tenant-boundary path). Pure advisory: it NEVER blocks (rc 0 always); it warns when owner-scoped routes ship with corner-6 unpinned. A repo with no owner-isolation, or a diff touching no handler, is a single clean row. | add a corner-6 boundary test asserting operator B's mutate of operator A's resource returns 404 (never 403 — that leaks existence; never 200) and the owner still succeeds. Pattern: daysout backend/handler/attraction_tenant_boundary_test.go. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `neutral-surface` | Operator-facing surfaces stay product-neutral. The factory dashboard must not link the operator to a product's SaaS subdomain (<product>.gyrum.ai). Surface the contract, docs, and changelog IN the dashboard (neutral /docs/..., /projects/... routes) from committed artifacts; the operator never leaves the dashboard. Server-side BFF fetches of committed artifacts are exempt. The gate is BLOCKING + DIFF-SCOPED: it refuses a PR only when a NEW (added in base...HEAD) operator-facing file (src/routes/**, src/lib/components/**, *.svelte) introduces an https://<product>.gyrum.ai link; a pre-existing line, a server-only file (+*.server.ts / proxy route), and any path in .gyrum/neutral-surface-allow.txt are exempt. | replace the https://<product>.gyrum.ai link with a dashboard-relative route (e.g. /docs/<product> or /projects/<product>) backed by a committed artifact, fetched server-side via a +page.server.ts or proxy route. Verify locally with `bash $DEVTOOLS/lib/neutral-surface-gate.sh --self-test <base-ref>`. For a deliberate, reviewed exception, add the file to .gyrum/neutral-surface-allow.txt and use the audited --skip-neutral-surface. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `regression-fixture` | bug-type PRs must include a regression test fixture that fails before the fix and passes after | add a test file (*_test.go, *.test.ts, *.test.sh, etc.) that exercises the bug path | `warp#3107` |
| `served-openapi` | a repo whose effective type OWES served-openapi (the `service` row of lib/type-gates-map.yaml — declared via repo-type.yaml `type: service` OR the ADR-093 `gates.profile: gyrum-service`), when a probe URL is available ($GYRUM_SERVICE_PROBE_URL or the gate's 2nd arg), runs a LIVE probe of its running server: GET /openapi.{yaml,json,yml} must return 200 and parse as a valid OpenAPI document (a mapping carrying `openapi:` + `paths:`), AND every concrete (parameter-free) path the served spec declares with a GET operation must not 404 on the live server (a 401/403/405/200/5xx all mean the route exists; only a 404 is a contradiction). A repo of any other / unknown type is a clean ✓ n/a row and is never probed (fail-closed on membership). An owing type with no probe URL configured is an advisory ⚠ row (rc 0) — the gate cannot probe a server that is not running. | make the running server serve its own in-repo OpenAPI spec at a stable path (/openapi.yaml) that parses as a valid OpenAPI document, and ensure every concrete GET path the spec declares is actually routed on the live server (no declared path 404s). Verify locally: `bash $DEVTOOLS/lib/served-openapi-gate.sh --self-test <repo-root> <base-url>` — it prints the gate row and exits 0 when the live server serves a valid spec and conforms. ai-research's cmd/server selfpublish (warp#9334, child-3) is the reference shape. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `service-surface` | a service repo (one that publishes an api/openapi.{yaml,yml,json} contract) surfaces the five contract-first standard surfaces (ADR-093): a service-index home page, an HTML OpenAPI (Redoc) view, a web-reachable changelog route (not just CHANGELOG.md on disk), request auth wired at the store/handler layer, and an append-only audit log. ADVISORY (rc 0, a ⚠ row) by default; BLOCKING (rc 1, ✗ + record_fail) under the gyrum-service repo-type profile (GYRUM_SERVICE_SURFACE_GATE_HARD=1, warp#8554) when a surface is missing. The gate detects both SvelteKit-page and Go-handler surface shapes (warp#8554). A repo with no OpenAPI contract is not a service — a single ✓ skipped row. | publish each absent surface: add the service-index page + the Redoc HTML-OpenAPI view + a web changelog route (Warp's reference set, warp#8469, and ai-research's cmd/server/selfpublish, warp#8544, are the templates), and wire store-layer auth + an audit log. Verify locally with `bash $DEVTOOLS/lib/service-surface-gate.sh --self-test <repo-root>` — it prints the presence map and exits 0 when all five are present. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `stories-coverage` | in a repo whose repo-type.yaml declares a design_system block, every canon-manifest.yaml owns[] entry of tier atom/molecule/organism has a co-located story file — same directory as the component, component basename with the extension swapped for .stories.ts (template/page tiers are out of scope) — i.e. `check-stories-coverage.sh --root . --check` reports 0 missing. With stories_coverage: warn (the default) the gate is advisory (exits 0); with stories_coverage: enforce a non-zero missing count exits 1. A repo with no design_system block or no canon-manifest.yaml is a clean no-op. | add the missing story: create <Component>.stories.ts next to the component (same dir, component basename) for every canon-manifest owns[] entry the gate lists, or drop the manifest entry if the component is gone. Check locally: `bash scripts/check-stories-coverage.sh --root . --check`. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-go-build` | the Go module compiles: `go build ./...` exits 0. | fix the compile error before pushing; run `go build ./...` locally. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-go-test` | `go test ./...` passes. ADVISORY in v1: red tests are surfaced but do not block (review-pr.sh warp#8033 v1). | fix the failing tests; run `go test ./...` locally. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-pr-shape` | a ticketed PR (branch matches feat/\|fix/\|chore/\|docs/\|refactor/ OR the body has a Closes/Fixes/Resolves warp#NNN close-verb) carries gyrum-start-work branch-meta (.gyrum/branch-meta/<branch>.json) whose ticket field is a valid warp#NNN matching the body close-verb — OR an audited .gyrum/branch-meta.no-ticket marker with a body that closes nothing. | create the branch via `gyrum-start-work <slug> --ticket warp#NNN` (writes the matching branch-meta) and keep the PR body close-verb aligned with that ticket; for genuinely-trivial work use `gyrum-start-work <slug> --no-ticket`; never improvise with `gh repo clone` / `git clone` / a manual branch + `gh pr create`. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-shellcheck` | every changed .sh file passes shellcheck with no findings (default severity). | run `shellcheck <file>` locally and fix each finding — quote variable expansions (SC2086), avoid echo\|grep under pipefail (SIGPIPE), prefer here-strings. Annotate a genuinely-false positive with a justified `# shellcheck disable=SCNNNN`. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-test-coverage` | the changed lines in the diff are covered at ≥ MIN_DIFF_COVERAGE (default 80%) by the test suite. | write a failing test first (TDD red), make it pass, then ship — cover each new branch, especially error paths; the test may live in a separate file from the source it covers. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
| `structural-token-duplication` | when a repo styles itself from @gyrum-labs/tokens, any local CSS custom-property declaration whose name matches the canonical name-set (resolved from the repo's own node_modules sheet, version-locked to what the app builds with) must carry an audited entry in devtools etc/token-brand-layer.yaml naming why it stays local (brand layer / staged family). | consume the token via var(--name) instead of re-declaring it, or add a reason-carrying entry to etc/token-brand-layer.yaml under the repo's key. Value equality is irrelevant — same NAME is the fork smell. | `warp#15535` |
| `structural-verification` | inside the existing PR `## Verification`, production UI screen/rendering changes require a renderable visual record; backend API/data/state/authority changes require a relevant flow, sequence or state diagram plus a boundary explanation, in addition to existing execution evidence. Root and nested module paths classify alike. Mixed changes require both; UI-only needs no backend diagram, backend-only needs no screen preview, and docs/tests/fixtures/unrelated scripts need neither visual shape. Existing advisory/enforce behaviour and audited exemptions stay unchanged. | UI: provide visual-kind (exactly design mockup, local compiled preview or deployed screenshot), artifact (Markdown image or functional-preview link), route or function, scenario, full-SHA source and caption; local artifacts must exist within the repo, match artifact-sha256 and the checked-out source HEAD. Backend: add a backend-diagram block with meaningful fenced Mermaid flow/sequence/state relationships and boundary explanation. Keep api-handler curl evidence, migration Before/After or schema-diff, CI actions/runs evidence and CLI invocation transcripts where required. Placeholders and bare spec filenames do not satisfy visuals. Remote records are supplied-not-fetched, not verified contents; reviewers judge relevance. Diagrams never replace execution proof. | `docs/shared/gate-stack.md` |
